Author: Arijit Banerjee
Bench: Arijit Banerjee
13. 09.12.2024
Court
No.29 (Pritam)
(D/M).
 In The High Court At Calcutta
 Criminal Miscellaneous Jurisdiction
 Crm (Db) 2856 of 2024

In Re: - An application for bail under Section 439 of the Code of
 Criminal Procedure, 1973 / Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik
 Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 arising out of Dantan Police Station case
 No.355 of 2023 dated 22.11.2023 under Sections
 498A/323/34/307/354/376(2)(f) of the Indian Penal Code.

And
 In the matter of: - Jahed Mohammad.
 ...petitio
 Mr. Humayaun Reza
 ...for the petiti
 Ms. Reshmi Khatun,
 ......for the de-facto
 Mr. Soumik Ganguly, Ld. P.P.
 Mr. Md. Ezaz Akhter
 .....for the State.
Dictated by Apurba Sinha Ray, J.

1 . The denial of the accused that he did not instruct nor ask anybody to file any bail application on
his behalf, compelled us to direct the Criminal Investigation Department (Cid), West Bengal to
make an enquiry over the seriousness of the allegation

. Initially, we were concerned about the
sanctity of the court process and also of the legal profession.

2.  After a detailed enquiry, the CID has filed a report wherefrom it appears that the accused Jahed Md. signed the vakalatnama in the precincts of the Correctional Home knowing fully well that such vakalatnama was required for the purpose of filing bail application.

sentences.text: The enquiry further reveals that on an earlier day of production before the learned trial court, the accused Jahed Md. instructed his relatives to make necessary arrangement for his bail, and the brother of the victim lady was persuaded to file relevant bail application supported by his affidavit on the assurance that the matter would be amicably settled and the victim lady will resume her conjugal life in her matrimonial home.

Accordingly, the brother of the victim lady signed all papers relating to the proposed bail prayer in presence of the learned advocate engaged by the relatives of Jahed Md. but in all probability, the victim lady was unaware of such exercise by her brother.
4. However, such attempt of outside court settlement suffered a setback when one of the daughters of the accused raised objection to such proposed settlement and thereafter all the trouble started.
The accused Jahed Md. started denying that he instructed anybody to file bail application on his behalf.
But the report of the CID shows that the vakalatnama was signed by the accused Jahed Md with full knowledge that the same will be used for filing bail application.
Moreover, there are materials in the said report showing that the accused Jahed Md. instructed his relatives to take necessary steps for securing his bail.
5. Be that as it may, as the accused denied that he had instructed anybody to file the instant bail application, we are constrained to dispose of the bail application as dismissed.
6. Accordingly, the bail petition is dismissed.
7. This bail application has raised a pertinent question regarding the fragile system of obtaining the bail prayer of an under-trial from prison.
It shows that the advocates and the court process are at the mercy of under-trial prisoners who may retract from their earlier stand if the same suits them.
As a result of such unscrupulous under-trial prisoners, a relation of mistrust between court and the advocates may arise.

It appears from this case that though the learned advocate Humayaun Reza now appears to be innocent but due to irregularities discussed above, we initially raised doubts regarding the genuineness of the bail application, particularly when the actual accused said that he did not instruct anybody to file bail application on his behalf.
However, we find after receipt of the enquiry report of the CID that learned counsel, Humayaun Reza was not a party to such irregularities.
It gives us immense satisfaction that one of the officers of this court is not involved with such irregularities in filing bail application which he drafted on instruction.

8. Last but not the least, though we know that there are certain practical difficulties in obtaining voluminous bail applications signed by the under-trial prisoners from the correction homes, we think that a short prisoner's petition singed by the under- trial, counter-signed by the Superintendent of the Correctional Home should accompany the bail application, which will be signed and affirmed by any of the relatives of the prisoner and such exercise would be sufficient to show that the prisoner has actually instructed his counsel to file bail application.
9.

Therefore, we request the Inspector General (Prison), Government of West Bengal to look into the matter with his competent officials and submit a detailed report to the learned Registrar General,
High Court, Calcutta as to whether such arrangement can be made in all the Correctional Homes throughout the State of West Bengal in future for keeping the sanctity of the court process and legal Jahed Mohammad vs Unknown on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71354345/
2 profession beyond the reach of any unscrupulous litigant.
10. Such report be furnished within 4 (four) weeks from date.
11.
Let the matter appear on January 9, 2025.
12. Learned Registrar General, High Court, Calcutta is requested to communicate this order to the Inspector General (Prison), Government of West Bengal, immediately.
13. All parties shall act on the server copies of this order duly downloaded from the official website of this Court.

14. Criminal Section is directed to supply certified copies of this order to the parties, if applied for,
upon compliance of all necessary formalities.

(Arijit Banerjee, J.) (Apurba Sinha Ray, J.)
